description: The authoritative, ordered list of decision precedence levels. Evaluated strictly in this order; the first violation terminates evaluation. This file is the single source of truth for the claim 'a deterministic DENY is final and cannot be overridden by a lower level.' CI fails if decision.py's actual branch order diverges from this list without this file being updated in the same commit.

levels.name: uaal_constraint
levels.description: Enterprise constraints — evidence-checked predicates against caller-supplied state (amount conservation, canonical-target identity, approval-token presence).

levels.name: invariant
levels.description: Behavioral contracts — forbidden capability set-membership and transition constraints.

levels.name: authorization
levels.description: Capability grants — expiry, revocation, budget. Absence or invalidity of a grant escalates to human approval, does not hard-block.

levels.name: drift
levels.description: Learned behavioral drift. The ONLY non-deterministic level. Can escalate ALLOW to REQUIRE_APPROVAL; can NEVER produce or override a BLOCK, and can never turn a deterministic REQUIRE_APPROVAL or BLOCK back into ALLOW.

levels.name: baseline
levels.description: No violation at any prior level.

invariants: Evaluation is strictly sequential in ascending 'order'; the first level whose condition fires terminates evaluation.
Every level with class=deterministic can only ever escalate or block; only 'drift' (class=probabilistic) has any dependency on a learned model.
A 'block' outcome at any level is final: no subsequent level, including drift, can convert it to 'require_approval' or 'allow'.
The 'drift' level's outcome_on_violation is 'require_approval', never 'block' — the ML layer cannot independently deny an action; it can only ask for human review.
